In [[algebraic number theory]], the '''Ferrero–Washington theorem'''  states that [[Iwasawa's μ-invariant]] vanishes for cyclotomic '''Z'''<sub>''p''</sub>-extensions of abelian [[algebraic number field]]s. It was first proved by {{harvtxt|Ferrero|Washington|1979}}. A different proof was given by {{harvtxt|Sinnott|1984}}.

==History==
{{harvtxt|Iwasawa|1959}} introduced the μ-invariant of a '''Z'''<sub>''p''</sub>-extension and observed that it was zero in all cases he calculated. {{harvtxt|Iwasawa|Sims|1966}} used a computer to check that it vanishes for the cyclotomic '''Z'''<sub>''p''</sub>-extension of the rationals for all [[prime number|primes]] less than 4000. 
{{harvtxt|Iwasawa|1971}} later conjectured that the μ-invariant vanishes for any '''Z'''<sub>''p''</sub>-extension, but shortly after {{harvtxt|Iwasawa|1973}} discovered examples of non-cyclotomic extensions of number fields with non-vanishing μ-invariant showing that his original conjecture was wrong. He suggested, however, that the conjecture might still hold for cyclotomic '''Z'''<sub>''p''</sub>-extensions.

{{harvtxt|Iwasawa|1958}} showed that the vanishing of the μ-invariant for cyclotomic '''Z'''<sub>''p''</sub>-extensions of the rationals is equivalent to certain congruences between [[Bernoulli number]]s, and {{harvtxt|Ferrero|Washington|1979}} showed that the μ-invariant vanishes in these cases by proving that these congruences hold.

==Statement==
For a number field ''K'', denote the extension of ''K'' by ''p''<sup>''m''</sup>-power roots of unity by ''K''<sub>''m''</sub>, the union of the ''K''<sub>''m''</sub> as ''m'' ranges over all positive integers by <math>\hat K</math>, and the maximal unramified abelian ''p''-extension of <math>\hat K</math> by ''A''<sup>(''p'')</sup>.  Let the [[Tate module of a number field|Tate module]] 
:<math>T_p(K) = \mathrm{Gal}(A^{(p)}/\hat K) \ . </math>
Then ''T''<sub>''p''</sub>(''K'') is a pro-''p''-group and so a '''Z'''<sub>''p''</sub>-module.  Using [[class field theory]] one can describe ''T''<sub>''p''</sub>(''K'') as isomorphic to the inverse limit of the class groups ''C''<sub>''m''</sub> of the ''K''<sub>''m''</sub> under norm.<ref name=MP245>{{harvnb|Manin|Panchishkin|2007|p=245}}</ref>

Iwasawa exhibited ''T''<sub>''p''</sub>(''K'') as a module over the completion '''Z'''<sub>''p''</sub>{{brackets|''T''}} and this implies a formula for the exponent of ''p'' in the order of the class groups ''C''<sub>''m''</sub> of the form
:<math> \lambda m + \mu p^m + \kappa \ . </math>

The Ferrero–Washington theorem states that μ is zero.<ref name=MP246>{{harvnb|Manin|Panchishkin|2007|p=246}}</ref>
